correctness.rationale: For i≠j the common neighbors of a_i and a_j are exactly B minus {b_i,b_j}, nonempty for n≥3. If at most two vertices of B are omitted from X, choose those two excluded indices (padding the pair if necessary); that distance-two pair fails. Conversely three omissions in B defeat every such obstruction, and analogously for A. Adjacent pairs require no internal vertex. For a_i,b_i the shortest length is three: choose omitted b_j with j≠i, then omitted a_k with k≠i,j, obtaining an X-avoiding interior. Thus the feasible choices are independent by part; their enumerator is the squared truncation, the top degree is 2n−6, and each maximal set leaves exactly three omissions per part, giving binom(n,3)^2. At n=3 the graph is C6 and only the empty set qualifies. The frozen verifier independently walks shortest paths by BFS distances for n=3,…,8 and its recorded replay covers 87360 subsets, including degree, coefficients and maximality. I inspected the code and recorded output, not executed it; the proof is unbounded.

evidence: The distance-two pairs of the crown are precisely the within-part pairs, with common neighborhoods obtained by deleting the two indexed vertices in the opposite part. These run over every (n−2)-subset, giving independent obstructions by side.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Apply the theorem and count all subsets of each part of size ≤n−3. Its top coefficient already counts all inclusion-maximal sets because every smaller part-size can be increased. No new distance-three lemma or separate counting argument is necessary.

evidence: Theorem 5.2 says N(u)∩N(v) must not be contained in X for each distance-two pair, i.e. X is independent in the hypergraph of these common neighborhoods.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalent hypergraph here is the disjoint union of two complete (n−2)-uniform hypergraphs; a set is independent iff it uses at most n−3 vertices per part. A transversal of every maximal geodesic is a different property.

originality.rationale: Bujtás–Klavžar–Tian, Theorem 5.2, already characterizes precisely these feasible sets in every connected graph by the distance-two common-neighborhood obstructions. On the crown these obstructions are all (n−2)-subsets of each part. Their independence conditions give exactly the claimed sets and all enumerations by direct counting. The original formula need not occur verbatim in the prior paper for this implication to cover it.
residual_risks: Searches were bounded. The linked Howroyd item was not separately retrieved; two further matching-deletion catalogue hits on ordinary visibility or edge-open packing were summary-only. The failure is based on the positive prior implication, not those gaps.
